lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Ah, hello again! Last night I wandered so far that I ended up lying on the grass, gazing at the <color=red>night sky</color>.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: It gave me three <color=red>riddles</color> about space. Solve all three and three new books will be sent to the library.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Now, where did I write them down? Aha, they were tucked inside my hat all along!

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: I am a planet that travels in an <color=red>orbit</color> around the sun. I have blue oceans and green land, and you are standing on me right now. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Where are you standing right now?
lines.correctText: Correct! It's the Earth, our home planet.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: I am a person who travels into space. I wear a <color=red>bulky</color> suit and a helmet so that I can breathe. Who am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these people goes into space?
lines.correctText: Yes! An astronaut travels into space.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I am a <color=red>frozen</color> lump of ice and dust. When I swoop close to the sun, I grow a long, glowing tail. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these is made of ice and dust and has a tail?
lines.correctText: Right! A comet has a glowing tail.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Three out of three! Your brain must be bigger than <color=red>Jupiter</color>. Three new books are on their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: Thank you for solving my riddles. If you spot a <color=red>shooting star</color> tonight, make a wish for me!
